summary: Tête-à-la-Baleine Airport (ZTB) is a small regional airstrip serving the remote coastal village of Tête-à-la-Baleine on Quebec's Lower North Shore, where road access does not exist. The community, whose name translates to "Head-to-the-Whale," relies on the airport as a vital link to the rest of Quebec and surrounding regions. It primarily handles small charter and regional flights connecting this isolated fishing village to larger hubs like Sept-Îles.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Tête-à-la-Baleine Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves the local community of Tête-à-la-Baleine, providing essential passenger and mail transport to a remote coastal village that has no road access.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to ZTB?
A: Scheduled service is limited and typically operated by small regional carriers using turboprop aircraft; travelers should check current schedules as routes to remote Lower North Shore communities can change seasonally.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small community airport, facilities are minimal, generally limited to a basic terminal building with no extensive amenities, food service, or car rentals on site.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Tête-à-la-Baleine?
A: Flying is often the only year-round option since the coastal ferry service is seasonal; however, summer months offer the most reliable weather and additional transport options.
transport_tips: There is no road connection to Tête-à-la-Baleine, so arriving by air via ZTB is typically the only year-round option for visitors. A seasonal ferry service connects the village to other Lower North Shore communities during summer months. Plan flights in advance and confirm transportation from the airport to your lodging, as rental cars are not available at the airstrip.
local_tip: Pack light and bring any specialty groceries or supplies with you, as the village has only a small general store with limited selection, and the nearest full-service shops are hundreds of kilometers away in Sept-Îles.
